quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. They tell drivers about road rules. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You use your left foot to operate it.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should prepare for:

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car can suddenly pull into traffic without warning. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and the parked cars.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
Checks performed only by a mechanic.
Service only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see ahead better. This also makes oncoming traffic more likely to see you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers can see you.
Ride offensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have small lights. Other drivers may not see you. Ride defensively and assume others cannot see you.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected by wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather or durable gloves protect your hands and give you better grip on the controls.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear too quickly, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
Front tire will likely skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When a group enters a curve, riders should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Use a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is used otherwise.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should NOT:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are slippery.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially important in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: The best lane position is one that:

options.text: Lets you travel the fastest.
Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Allows other motorists to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that allows others to see you and gives you space to move. Avoid blind spots and surface hazards. Discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and have an escape route ready.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should let others see you and provide enough space to move safely.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Give you an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, avoid wind blasts, and stay out of blind spots. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than usual.
Apply the brakes gently.
Not use the rear brake.
Not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, apply the brakes gently and with caution.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean their shoulders with the turn angle.
Sit as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight when riding.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight when riding.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight makes you more visible at intersections. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can react to dangers. Do not rely only on eye contact with drivers—they may not notice you.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Jacket
Boots
Gloves
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding. Sandals do not protect you.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down unexpectedly, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire is flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually will not hear a tire fail.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Ride straight ahead. If you must brake, gradually apply it only to the tire that is not flat. Slowly move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen in legal passing zones. Follow posted speed limits and only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If a tire is flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire is flat and you must brake, gradually apply the brake only to the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on a slippery surface. Apply the front brake gradually to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: What best reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Riding on the shoulder
Riding under the speed limit
Wearing a helmet
Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase speed before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from leaning.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: The front brake only.
The rear brake only.
Both front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Engine braking:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is slowing down by turning the engine off.
Is slowing down by downshifting.
Is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows you down like braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders for a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is often caused by:

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Not knowing how to steer.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means another driver will properly yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them.
Encourage them to use quiet roads.
Not get involved.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Take their keys if needed. Arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is recommended.
Can cause hearing loss.
Is not harmful.
Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding:

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
There will be no change in steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, safely exit the road and check your tires.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes right away.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by closing the throttle, lean forward, and pull off the road safely. Do not brake suddenly, as this can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: They should lean together at the same angle.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays upright.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body straight.

questions.question: If you need to brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are no longer turning to brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when leaning than when upright. Always try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake in a turn, apply brakes smoothly and gently, not hard.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is usually the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash, regardless of speed.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by closing the throttle. If you must brake, gradually use the brake on the good tire. Steer carefully to the roadside, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When someone is passing you from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is the rule?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish the pass in a no-passing zone if you started before it.
You can exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within the speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.
